[[File:Jordans inequality.svg|thumb|upright=1.2|[[unit circle]] with angle x and a second circle with radius <math>|EG|=\sin(x)</math> around E. <math>\begin{align}&|DE|\leq|\widehat{DC}|\leq|\widehat{DG}|\\ \Leftrightarrow &\sin(x) \leq x \leq\tfrac{\pi}{2}\sin(x)\\ \Rightarrow &\tfrac{2}{\pi}x \leq \sin(x)\leq x  \end{align}</math>]]

In mathematics, '''Jordan's inequality''', named after [[Camille Jordan]], states that<ref>{{MathWorld|title=Jordan's inequality|urlname=JordansInequality}}</ref>

: <math>\frac{2}{\pi}x\leq \sin(x) \leq x\text{ for }x \in \left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right].</math>

It can be proven through the [[geometry]] of [[circles]] (see drawing).<ref>Feng Yuefeng, Proof without words: Jordan`s inequality, Mathematics Magazine, volume 69, no. 2, 1996, p. 126</ref>
